title: Diamond Intel
overview: An advanced predictive modeling platform for the gemstone market. Powered by a CatBoost gradient boosted decision tree model, it estimates statistically robust diamond market values — with confidence-bounded price ranges for both buyers and sellers.

content.text:
**Diamond Intel** was developed as an **ML Course Final Project** by a team of three:

• **Kasun Vishvajith** — ML modelling, CatBoost pipeline, prediction interval system & application architecture.
• **Isuru Dulakshana** — Feature engineering, data preprocessing & Normal model development.
• **Gayani Wathsala** — Exploratory data analysis, clarity/color encoding & evaluation metrics.

The core problem we tackled: **pricing diamonds accurately is non-trivial**. The relationships between carat weight, geometric dimensions, and visual quality grades are deeply **non-linear** — making simple regression models unreliable. This project applies **gradient boosted decision trees** to output statistically robust, confidence-bounded valuation ranges.

The predictive application runs in **three core steps**:

• **Enter Specifications**: Input physical traits like **Carat, Color, Clarity**, and exact millimeter dimensions (**X, Y, Z**). The model supports **Natural/Lab-Grown Diamonds** and **Cubic Zirconia** simulants.
• **Process & Analyze**: The CatBoost engine evaluates multi-dimensional feature interactions using **deep decision trees**. Choose between the **Normal model** (7 features) or the **Advanced model** (10 features) for higher precision.
• **Get Market Range**: Instead of a single price point, you receive a **statistically bounds-checked prediction** at either 90% or 95% confidence. Ranges are adjusted based on whether you are acting as a **Buyer** or a **Seller**.

To support scenarios where full geometric data is unavailable, we built **two distinct model tiers**:

• **Normal Model** — Uses **7 core features**: Type, X, Y, Z, Carat, Clarity, and Color. An excellent baseline when cut proportions are unknown. Confidence interval: **±13% std error** in log-space.
• **Advanced Model** — Incorporates **all 10 features**, adding **Cut Grade, Table %, and Depth %**. Delivers the highest precision with **tighter confidence bounds** (±7% std error in log-space) by fully exploiting proportion geometry.

Each of the **10 input features** captures a distinct physical or optical property of the stone:

• **Type**: Natural/Lab Diamond vs Cubic Zirconia. Diamonds command a **massive rarity premium** — reflected directly in the model's log-price intercept.
• **Carat**: Physical mass of the diamond (1 ct = 0.2 g). Price scales **exponentially** — a 2 ct stone costs far more than 2× a 1 ct stone.
• **Measurements (X, Y, Z)**: Length, Width, and Depth in millimetres. Determines **apparent visual size** and governs **light path through the facets**.
• **Color Grade**: Colorless purity scale from **D (premium colorless)** to **J (near colorless)**. The model encodes grades D–J.
• **Clarity Grade**: Absence of internal inclusions, from **IF (Internally Flawless)** to **I1 (Inclusions visible to the naked eye)**.
• **Cut Grade**: Facet alignment quality — **Ideal, Premium, Very Good, Good, Fair**. Ideal cuts maximize light return and brilliance.
• **Depth %**: Z ÷ average diameter (X+Y)/2. **Ideal range: ~59% to 62.5%**. Stones outside this range lose brilliance as light leaks.
• **Table %**: Width of the flat top facet ÷ average diameter. **Ideal range: ~54% to 57%**. Extremes dull the stone's scintillation.

Beyond the ML predictor, the app ships **three standalone proportion tools** for manual gem analysis:

• **Carat ↔ Grams Converter**: Instantly translate between carat weight and grams (1 ct = 0.2 g).
• **Depth % Calculator**: Input X, Y, Z dimensions to compute Z ÷ average(X,Y) — with an **Ideal / Shallow / Deep** quality badge.
• **Table % Calculator**: Input table width and diameter to compute the table ratio — with **Ideal / Narrow / Wide** assessment.

Diamond prices exhibit **exponential variance** — a 5-carat stone isn't 5× more expensive than a 1-carat stone, it can be 20×. To model this correctly, we train on the **natural logarithm of price** rather than raw price:

• **Training target**: LogPrice = ln(Price) — this linearises the exponential relationship and stabilises model variance across all carat categories.
• **Inference**: Final Price = exp(LogPrice) — we exponentiate the prediction to recover the dollar value.
• **Prediction Intervals**: Computed as symmetric log-space deltas — exp(LogPrice ± z·σ) — where z = 1.645 for 90% bounds and z = 1.96 for 95% bounds. This ensures intervals **widen naturally** for high-value stones.
